synonyms: Desmanthus depressus Humb. & Bonpl. ex Willd. (treated as synonym in ITIS)
look_here_first: Often spreading to ascending perennial/subshrub; bipinnate leaves and small whitish heads with NARROW mostly straighter pods (often 30–80 × 3–5 mm). Habit is variable; confirm species with a full leaf, gland, flower heads and mature pods. Do not mistake D. virgatus var. acuminatus for this accepted species.

morphology_keys.growth_flower_fruit: Highly variable perennial/subshrub, often sprawling to ascending or erect; smaller off-white brushlike flower heads. Many slender narrow pods may radiate from a head; vegetation and pod dimensions overlap relatives. The broad D. virgatus complex has been taxonomically unstable.
morphology_keys.distinguishing_characters: Not the broad sickle pods of Illinois. D. acuminatus was formerly D. virgatus var. acuminatus but is accepted separately. Use voucher-level combination of whole shoot, stem hair, leaf/gland, flower and pod, especially in Central Texas.
morphology_keys.shared_genus: Unarmed perennial Fabaceae with compound bipinnate leaves and small brushlike heads, often a petiolar/rachis gland, flat legume pods. Pod structure diagnostic.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Not the broad sickle pods of Illinois. D. acuminatus was formerly D. virgatus var. acuminatus but is accepted separately. Use voucher-level combination of whole shoot, stem hair, leaf/gland, flower and pod, especially in Central Texas.
